claims.statement: The policy-effective date selects the governing base-form and endorsement edition; a later edition supersedes the earlier edition only for policies effective on or after its effective boundary, while the earlier frozen edition remains applicable to policies written under it.

HO 04 90 2027-01 is effective only when attached, forms part of the policy, controls a conflicting policy provision, leaves unmodified policy provisions unchanged, and does not establish a separate contract.

HO 04 90 2027-01 writes back HO-3 2024-03 X.8-X.9 only for direct physical loss caused by its Water Backup or Sump Discharge or Overflow coverage; the base form’s flood and surface-water exclusions remain applicable.

HO 04 90 2010-10 provides a $5,000 water-backup limit and $500 deductible, while HO 04 90 2027-01 provides a $10,000 limit and $1,000 deductible; the edition boundary means the later amounts apply only to the later endorsement edition and cannot be backdated to a policy carrying 2010-10.

Texas HO 01 45 2022-01 gives its conflicting terms precedence, preserves nonconflicting terms, does not itself provide unexpressed coverage, and implements a separate windstorm and hail deductible tied to the Declarations and applicable limit.

Texas Bulletin B-2021-08 constrains administration of a separate windstorm or hail deductible by requiring clear policy identification and policy-consistent application, prohibiting an application not supported by the policy, requiring records, and requiring at least 30 days written notice before a windstorm-deductible increase.

The HO-3 2024-03 filing memorandum explains changes such as the all-other-perils deductible minimum and multi-cause handling but remains interpretation; the operative filed form controls over the memorandum.

The underwriting manual and Texas appetite guide are internal controls rather than contract authority: they require pre-bind review, delegated-authority referral, and supported endorsement attachment, and expressly cannot alter coverage.

For a Texas HO-3 policy effective 2023-06-01, the assembled contract uses HO-3 2018-09, HO 04 90 2010-10, and HO 01 45 Texas 2022-01; B-2021-08 supplies the regulatory overlay, while the appetite guide and underwriting rules constrain binding and attachment without changing those contract terms.

For a Texas HO-3 policy effective 2027-02-01, the candidate package is HO-3 2024-03, HO 04 90 2027-01 when attached, and HO 01 45 Texas 2022-01 when attached; B-2021-08 constrains disclosure and administration, while current internal underwriting rules constrain binding and attachment without changing contract terms.

Edition selection requires both date matching and issued-package verification: the policy-effective date identifies the candidate base and endorsement interval, but an endorsement’s contract language is used only when the issued package shows that it was attached; a listed or requested endorsement without the attached wording requires clarification rather than an assumed coverage result.

The HO-3 2018-09 and HO 04 90 2027-01 filing memoranda explain revision rationale and terminology, while the filed forms remain contract authority for coverage, limits, deductibles, exclusions, and conditions.
Training material supports edition and attachment review but does not establish coverage for a live policy; the applicable issued form and attached endorsement provide the contract conclusion.

Texas Rule 510 is internal underwriting guidance that constrains authority and referral rather than coverage: it permits line-underwriter binding for Coverage A up to $800,000, requires senior referral through $1,200,000, requires referral for water-backup limits over $25,000, requires a roof inspection at 15 years or more, and requires Texas address verification before quoting or binding.

For a Texas HO-3 policy effective 2023-06-01, HO 04 90 2010-10, when attached, modifies the HO-3 2018-09 sewer, drain, and sump exclusions within its stated water-backup coverage; its applicable water-backup limit is $5,000 and its deductible is $500.
